name: Columite-GX
description: A silicon nitride–tungsten carbide structural ceramic developed as a direct replacement for construction-grade steel, offering comparable tensile strength at forty percent of the weight with far superior corrosion and thermal resistance. The microstructure is engineered through nano-assembly to include elongated beta-silicon nitride grains that act as crack deflectors, giving Columite-GX a fracture toughness unusually high for a ceramic — approaching that of cast iron. Crucible Industries markets it aggressively for megastructure construction where cumulative dead load reduction translates to significant engineering advantages.
story_hooks: A structural survey reveals that load-bearing Columite-GX members in a Tier 2 residential tower have been substituted with counterfeit material — the building houses ten thousand people and the columns are already showing micro-fractures.

Crucible Industries has been quietly testing a new Columite-GX formulation in the foundations of Tier 3 district infrastructure without disclosure — and the long-term behavior of the experimental mix is unknown.

A demolitions team needs to bring down a Columite-GX reinforced structure quietly — the material's fracture toughness makes conventional explosives inefficient, and they need a materials specialist who knows its specific failure modes.
